title: अध्याय ६७

items.speaker: मार्कण्डेय उवाच
items.text:
ततः स्वारोचिषं नाम्ना द्युतिमन्तं प्रजापतिम् ।
मनुं चकार भगवांस्तस्य मन्वन्तरं शृणु ॥ १ ॥
items.tr:
tataḥ svārociṣaṃ nāmnā dyutimantaṃ prajāpatim |
manuṃ cakāra bhagavāṃstasya manvantaraṃ śṛṇu || 1 ||

items.text:
तत्रान्तरे तु ये देवा मुनयस्तत्सुताश्च ये ।
भूपालाः क्रौष्टुके ये तान्गदतस्त्वं निशामय ॥ २ ॥
items.tr:
tatrāntare tu ye devā munayastatsutāśca ye |
bhūpālāḥ krauṣṭuke ye tāngadatastvaṃ niśāmaya || 2 ||

items.text:
देवाः पारावतास्तत्र तथैव तुषिता द्विज ।
स्वारोचिषेऽन्तरे चेन्द्रो विपश्चिदिति विश्रुतः ॥ ३ ॥
items.tr:
devāḥ pārāvatāstatra tathaiva tuṣitā dvija |
svārociṣe'ntare cendro vipaściditi viśrutaḥ || 3 ||

items.text:
ऊर्जस्तम्बस्तथा प्राणो दत्तोऽलिर्ऋषभस्तथा ।
निश्चरश्चार्ववीरश्च तत्र सप्तर्षयोऽभवम् ॥ ४ ॥
items.tr:
ūrjastambastathā prāṇo datto'lirṛṣabhastathā |
niścaraścārvavīraśca tatra saptarṣayo'bhavam || 4 ||

items.text:
तस्य मन्वन्तरं यावत्तावत्तद्वंशविस्तरे ।
भुक्तेयमवनिः सर्वा द्वितीयं वै तदन्तरम् ॥ ६ ॥
items.tr:
tasya manvantaraṃ yāvattāvattadvaṃśavistare |
bhukteyamavaniḥ sarvā dvitīyaṃ vai tadantaram || 6 ||

items.text:
स्वरोचिषस्तु चरितं जन्म स्वारोचिषस्य च ।
निशम्य मुच्यते पापैः श्रद्धधानो हि मानवः ॥ ७ ॥
items.tr:
svarociṣastu caritaṃ janma svārociṣasya ca |
niśamya mucyate pāpaiḥ śraddhadhāno hi mānavaḥ || 7 ||

en_summary: Markandeya tells Kraushtuki that the Lord then made Dyutiman, called Svarochisha, a Prajapati and the Manu, and describes his period (manvantara): its gods, sages, sons and kings. In the Svarochisha period the gods were the Paravatas and the Tushitas, and the Indra was the famous Vipashchit. The seven sages were Urja, Stamba, Prana, Datta, Ali (as printed), Rishabha, Nishchara and Arvavira (the list as printed names eight). Chaitra, Kimpurusha and others were the seven very powerful sons of the great Manu, who ruled the earth. As long as his period lasted, the whole earth was enjoyed by his widespread family; this was the second Manu period. A person of faith who hears the story of Svarochis and the birth of Svarochisha is freed from sins.
